_comment: Conversation states and the ordered rules that pick one. Rules are evaluated top to bottom; the first that matches wins. If none matches the state is 'unknown': the engine never guesses. Only the first rule is verified (it uses the ticket state Node supplies); the others are inferences from the message flow and are flagged for review.

states.description: The ticket is recorded as resolved or closed by the system.
The customer wrote last and asked for something; the next move is support's.
Support wrote last and asked the customer for something; the next move is the customer's.
A problem the customer reported is still open, but whose turn it is cannot be determined.
There is not enough evidence to say.

resolvedTicketStatuses.note: The 'done' status used by the ticket views.
Ticket state produced by the Node ticket-state mapping when isComplete is true.

rules.justification: Verified: Node reports isComplete or a terminal status. This is the only rule that relies on system data, not on interpreting messages.
No customer or support message to reason about.
The agent inbox already treats a customer message without a later reply as waiting for support (unread indicator, last-message preview).
A customer saying thanks may be closing the matter or not; the engine does not decide.
The existing outbound templates ask the customer to update or upload documents; a later reply is expected from the customer.
The customer reported a problem, support replied without asking for anything, and nothing says it was fixed.
The customer wrote last and reported a problem, even without an explicit question.
